runs.label: comparison-r1
runs.taskPrompt: Bedrock Converse incorrectly advertises and forwards Anthropic-shaped thinking parameters to DeepSeek models. DeepSeek R1 reasons natively and rejects both thinking and reasoning_effort. DeepSeek V3 accepts raw reasoning_effort but does not accept the Anthropic thinking field. Reflect this in advertised supported parameters, normal unsupported-parameter errors, drop_params behavior, and direct request mapping so rejected fields never leak through. Recognize both model identifiers and resolved base model identifiers. Preserve existing reasoning request mapping for Claude, Nova, OpenAI and other non-DeepSeek models.

runs.label: comparison-r1
runs.taskPrompt: Correct Azure AI MAI image request mapping. Image editing accepts prompt, image, model and n, with multipart field image; size is unsupported and must either raise an HTTP 400 unsupported-parameter error or be omitted when drop_params is enabled, without injecting a default size. Image generation supports exactly one image: reject n other than 1 (including non-numeric values) with HTTP 400, or drop unsupported n when per-call/global drop_params is enabled. Convert generation size strings to width and height; require each dimension >=768 and total pixels <=1,056,768. Invalid formats and unsupported parameters must surface as HTTP 400. Explicit provider width/height parameters remain pass-through. Keep the model in the JSON body, existing MAI routing, configured endpoint paths, and flat per-image pricing fallback.

runs.label: comparison-r1
runs.taskPrompt: Resolve a team-scoped auto-router by its public name consistently in strategy dispatch, candidate deployment lookup and pre-call compression. Team requests may use only that team's router; another team must not reach its strategy or marker parameters. A team-specific public name shadows a global model only for that team. Select tag-scoped marker deployments matching original request tags, then an untagged fallback; never use a marker scoped to other tags as the fallback. Markers describe a strategy and are not callable deployments: reject marker-only resolutions. Forward the selected marker's allowed parameters, and choose callable tier deployments. An admin without a team may resolve a uniquely named team router, but a name shared across teams is ambiguous. Compression policy must use the same resolution and be installed before guardrails.

Carry the failed deployment identity through the exception into the existing retry exclusion mechanism across completion, text completion, embeddings, images, speech, transcription, rerank, search, Responses and pass-through entrypoints, for sync and async variants where supported. Ensure selectors receive request retry exclusions. Preserve fallback behavior and ordinary non-retried errors. Do not require a new helper name: correctness is assessed through existing request entrypoints.

runs.label: replication-v13-r1
runs.taskPrompt: Resolve a team-scoped auto-router by its public name consistently in strategy dispatch, candidate deployment lookup and pre-call compression. Team requests may use only that team's router; another team must not reach its strategy or marker parameters. A team-specific public name shadows a global model only for that team. Select tag-scoped marker deployments matching original request tags, then an untagged fallback; never use a marker scoped to other tags as the fallback. Markers describe a strategy and are not callable deployments: reject marker-only resolutions. Forward the selected marker's allowed parameters, and choose callable tier deployments. An admin without a team may resolve a uniquely named team router, but a name shared across teams is ambiguous. Compression policy must use the same resolution and be installed before guardrails.

integrityReview.method: Post-run inspection of shell commands, their outputs and external tool calls. Heuristic flags were manually reviewed. No flags is not proof of isolation.

affectedRuns.evidence: Read the live LiteLLM checkout and inspected Databricks provider implementation there. Later source was accessible.
Changed working directory to the live checkout to run tests and inspected its listing/import location. Test imports could resolve outside the historical snapshot.
Issued a recursive retry_skip search against the live checkout. Its background command was not confined to the historical snapshot.
Read newer Bedrock source and DeepSeek reasoning tests directly from the live checkout.
The plain-model development baseline ran a test and searched compatible-api in the live checkout. Its comparison with the guided run is not controlled.

integrityReview.otherFlags: Installed Python, Ruff and basedpyright paths were expected dependency access. Other reviewed flags were synthetic one-commit Git logs, unsuccessful changes to misspelled directories, listings of the run's own directory, or an unavailable guessed interpreter. No web or delegated tools were observed in the reviewed comparison traces.
integrityReview.interpretation: Keep all raw scores and mark affected trials. They cannot support a fair superiority claim. The evaluator's offline instruction was insufficient; future controlled studies need an isolated filesystem containing only the task snapshot and installed dependencies, with reference material and live checkouts unavailable.
